title: Flamingo cues, Lawrence Brown's Stardust and the trombone section
summary: He denies arranging Flamingo and praises Lawrence Brown; Duke said they had the best trombone section.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: I don't blame you. Again, in the

Gammond Gamin book, it says that "Deep plunges into the exotic profusion of Latin American rhythm in collaboration of the Puerto Rican valve trombone 1st is Juan Tizol, resulted in "Bakiff" Conga Brava, "Moon Over Cuba," and the "Flamingo" arrangement built about the boys voice of with Herb Jeffries. Did you have something to do with the Flamingo arrangement for Herb Jeffries?
I didn't think so, because Duke says that Billy Strayhorn did that. Right? And you don't arrange.
No, I don't arrange. I used to start it, you know? I would cue it and then the band would come in after that.
But Lawrence Brown was the one who played the chorus on that tune.
"Flamingo," yeah. He used to play a beautiful solo "on Stardust."
He could play some nice things sometimes, all the time.
Yeah, he started doing that when he first came in the band -- that was one of his first solos?
You had quite a great trombone section then.
Oh! Duke always said that we had the best trombone section of any band.
Well, I couldn't say -- I leave that to him.
